projects.name: projects

attributes.title: Contract-Advisor-RAG
attributes.summary: I have developed a contract assistant chatbot that allows users to upload contract documents and then chat with the chatbot about the contents of those documents. The chatbot is built using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) system, and I have explored different strategies for implementing the RAG system, including a simple RAG approach, a multi-query approach, and an auto-generation approach. I have evaluated the performance of these different strategies using the RAGAS evaluation metric, and have implemented the best performing strategy in my final chatbot system.

attributes.title: Crypto-Trading-Engineering
attributes.summary:
In this project, we used large language models (LLMs) for time series data prediction related to cryptocurrency investments. First, we conducted backtesting to evaluate different investment strategies and identify the most effective approach. We then applied modern portfolio theory to create an optimized set of cryptocurrency investments to maximize the overall investment returns. Next, we utilized two time series models for predicting the closing prices of cryptocurrency coins. The first model was Moirai-1.0-R-large, which is a specialized time series model. The second model was Chronos, which is a framework for adapting large language models to handle time series forecasting tasks.

To evaluate the performance of these two time series models, we prepared training and test datasets from the historical cryptocurrency data. By applying these two models to the test data, we were able to generate predictions for the future closing prices of the cryptocurrency coins.

attributes.title: Logistic optimization: Delivery drivers location optimisation with Causal Inference
attributes.summary: As the largest last-mile delivery service in Nigeria, Gokada has completed over a million deliveries in less than a year with a fleet of over 1,200 riders. However, Gokada has faced a key challenge - the sub-optimal placement of their drivers (which they call "pilots") and clients, leading to a high number of unfulfilled delivery requests. To address this, Gokada asked me to help them understand the primary causes of these unfulfilled requests and come up with solutions that recommend driver locations to increase the fraction of complete orders. Since Gokada's drivers are paid based on the number of requests they accept, the solution will help Gokada's business grow both in terms of client satisfaction and increased business. To tackle this, I used the CausalNex library to uncover the structural relationships in Gokada's data, including environmental factors like weather and holidays, as well as the day of the week (weekday vs. weekend) and the distance between the customer and driver locations obtained through a free API. This allowed me to learn complex distributions and use the DoWhy library to estimate causal effects, quantify causal influence, and perform root cause analysis. This combined approach enabled me to provide Gokada with deep insights and actionable recommendations to optimize their driver placement and increase their delivery completion rate.
